entry.title: Bitcoin Core v31.3 Released
entry.summary:
Bitcoin Core version 31.3 introduces a series of bug fixes, performance enhancements, and updated translations, further refining the stability and usability of the software. Users are encouraged to download the latest release from [https://bitcoincore.org/bin/bitcoin-core-31.3/](https://bitcoincore.org/bin/bitcoin-core-31.3/) and to report any bugs encountered using the issue tracker available at [https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues). Additional community discussions and announcements can be accessed through [https://bitcoincore.org/en/list/announcements/join/](https://bitcoincore.org/en/list/announcements/join/).
Upgrading to version 31.3 requires users running older versions to first shut down their current instance of Bitcoin Core, waiting until it is fully closed before proceeding with the installation process. On Windows, the installer should be executed; on macOS, the `/Applications/Bitcoin-Qt` file should be replaced; and on Linux, the `bin/` and `libexec/` directories should be overwritten. Upgrading directly from an end-of-life (EOL) version is supported, although migration may take longer if the data directory requires updating. Legacy wallet formats remain generally compatible with this release.
The software maintains official support and thorough testing for Linux Kernel 3.17 or newer, macOS 14 or newer, and Windows 10 (version 1903) or newer. While Bitcoin Core typically operates on other Unix-like systems, these platforms do not receive the same level of testing and support, making it inadvisable to rely on unsupported environments.
Version 31.3 contains several notable improvements. The networking component now processes only unique transaction inventory messages (tx INVs), enhancing efficiency. Continuous integration workflows have also been optimized by introducing inline runner selection and leveraging Docker BuildKit caching mechanisms.
Acknowledgement is given to direct contributors Greg Sanders and willcl-ark, as well as to those who assisted with translation efforts, underscoring the collaborative nature of this open-source project.
